M-DIAGRAM:
Export the docs graph as deterministic Archify architecture IR, a dependency-free Mermaid flowchart, or standalone HTML rendered by the optional Archify CLI (ADR-9), with a machine receipt and an IR staleness gate. src/grace-diagram.ts M-COMMON,M-CONFIG,M-ERRORS,M-INTEGRATIONS,M-LINT,M-SHARD,M-TEST,M-XML V-M-DIAGRAM
<export-diagramCommand PURPOSE="mygrace diagram [--kind architecture] [--format text|json|html|mermaid] [--out ] [--quality standard|showcase] [--check]; JSON/Mermaid need no Archify, HTML requires validated/delivered Archify." />
<CrossLink to="M-INTEGRATIONS" relation="Archify detection, pinned tested range (>=3.2 <4) and scrubbed child env come from ADR-9 registry" />
Render the machine graph for humans without hand-authored diagrams: the docs graph is the single source of truth and the generated IR is committed and checked.
<param name="out" type="string?" description="Project-relative .html path; default /architecture.html." />
Archify validates "clean flow": a dense module graph cannot be auto-routed without edges crossing nodes, so HTML shows a legible primary-dependency backbone (one edge per module, dependency-depth layers). JSON and Mermaid always carry the full declared graph; the receipt records declared vs depicted counts. Determinism: components/connections/boundaries/cards are sorted, layout is computed from labels and dependency depth, and the graph sha256 covers only graph inputs — repeated runs produce byte-identical IR. ADR-9: allowlisted `archify validate/deliver` only, argv-only with scrubbed env, timeout from config, output parsed as untrusted JSON; nothing runs during lint/ci. Tested against Archify CLI 3.2.0 (bundled in @tt-a1i/archify-dsh@1.1.0) and 3.3.x (1.2.0); full-binary smoke is manual (`bun run test:integrations:archify`). v1.5.0 ships `--kind architecture`; workflow/tree kinds remain follow-ups.
